meta.bit_reading_note: Part A positions (part W) run the wait test on the label's chain: classical bits c0 to c4 are the end lines' results, in the order L1, L3, L1, L3, L1 (manacitra.wait.WAIT_TEST_ROUNDS), and c5 is M's; Part B (part B): classical bit i is the i-th qubit of the label's qubits
meta.description: Kickoff 49, the wait test on a second day: Kickoff 48 run again with its rule unchanged. Part A: the wait test (manacitra.wait.build_wait_test) on Kickoff 48's five chains L1-M-L3, 144-143-142, 143-144-145, 141-142-143, 132-131-138 and 125-124-123, each without and with XY4 refocusing pulses, 4 interleaved copies of 5000 shots. Part B: Ramsey and echo (manacitra.wait.part_b) on Kickoff 47's groups, {143, 131, 124} and {142, 144, 125}, at eight waits from 0 to 4000 dt (0 to 16 us), the circuit's own wait T_M among them, each circuit twice, 2000 shots each. 104 circuits in one job, the two parts interleaved; the sampler's own dynamical decoupling and twirling off, as IBM recorded them.
meta.bit_order: Qiskit bitstrings, rightmost character = classical bit 0

built_from.how: every circuit built by manacitra.wait at this commit (the v0.5.0 tag), unedited: Part A by build_wait_test(chain, refocus, backend), translated at optimization level 0 with the chain as the layout, XY4 by refocused; Part B by part_b and to_backend; against the live ibm_fez target at build (dt 4 ns, granularity 1)
built_from.rebuild: manacitra.wait at this commit rebuilds every circuit from the chains, groups and waits here; tests/test_wait.py rebuilds them for the offline ibm_fez snapshot and checks them against cells, part_B_circuits and offline_build

T_M.definition: end of M's first H (its first sx) to the start of its last H (its last sx), scheduled without refocusing

offline_build.what: the dry run before the go: the same circuits built for qiskit-ibm-runtime's offline ibm_fez snapshot, whose durations differ from the live target's (measure plus reset 786 dt, against 836 live), so its T_M, waits and refocusing pulses differ; not sent

fixed_before_the_data.rule: H48: F_pred = F_ref x (1 - dP_R(T_M)), dP_R(T_M) = P_R(T_M) - P_R(0) on M, the Ramsey P(1) pooled over Part B's two copies; d_M = F_no - F_pred, its 90% interval from a joint bootstrap of both parts. DISAGREE if any chain's d_M interval lies entirely outside [-margin, +margin]; AGREE if every chain's lies entirely inside; NOT SETTLED otherwise. A chain is informative if its dP_R(T_M) interval lies entirely above the informative floor; with none, the verdict carries ', uninformative'
fixed_before_the_data.F_classes: LOW if the 90% interval lies entirely below 0.3, HIGH if entirely above 0.6, MIDDLE otherwise
fixed_before_the_data.part_b_rule: manacitra.wait.part_b_losses at the reference wait, with its default thresholds (Kickoff 47's rule)
fixed_before_the_data.bootstraps: Part A: copies with replacement within each cell, each redrawn from a multinomial (seed bootstrap_A); Part B: manacitra.wait.part_b_losses (seed bootstrap_B); the prediction: both parts jointly, in a fixed order, chains in meta.chains order, for each F_no then F_ref (Part A's draw), then P_R(T_M) and P_R(0) (Part B's draw) (seed joint)

analyse_49.py.text:
"""Kickoff 49 analysis, fixed before the data: Kickoff 48 section 2, unchanged, computed by the repository's own code.

The verdict comes from the Kickoff 48 recompute in Manacitra's tests/_reuse_runs.py (k48_wait_test), exported unedited
at a55354d into hardware-49/src-a55354d, with manacitra.wait from hardware-49/site. The only adaptation is the file
names: this script reads Kickoff 49's submit and counts files and hands them to k48_wait_test in the shape of the
repository's data record (meta, fixed_before_the_data, labels, counts), so that Kickoff 48 and Kickoff 49 are computed
the same way.

H48's rule, word for word: DISAGREE if any chain's d_M interval lies entirely outside [-0.15, +0.15]; AGREE if every
chain's lies entirely inside; NOT SETTLED otherwise. A chain is informative if its dP_R(T_M) interval lies entirely above
0.2; with none, the verdict is written "uninformative".

Seeds (inputs.json): joint 49 (the verdict's bootstrap); bootstrap_A 4949043 and bootstrap_B 4949 for the per-part
intervals reported beside it.

Beside the verdict, not used by it: each qubit's Kickoff 47 kind at 3.4 us; whether 143's offset is still there, with
the package's fit labelled as a fit; the oscillation sign on 143; each chain's d_M beside Kickoff 48's; the calibration
stamps at build, submission and fetch beside Kickoff 48's.

Usage: python analyse_49.py              (Kickoff 49's files)
       python analyse_49.py --selftest   (Kickoff 48's files and seeds through the same path; must give results-48.json)"""
from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import json
import sys
import time
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(HERE / "site"))
sys.path.insert(0, str(HERE / "src-a55354d" / "tests"))
from manacitra import wait as W  # noqa: E402
import _reuse_runs as reuse  # noqa: E402

K48_DIR = HERE.parent / "hardware-48"
CAL_K48_UTC = datetime(2026, 10, 11, 1, 35, tzinfo=timezone.utc)


def sha(p):
    return hashlib.sha256(Path(p).read_bytes()).hexdigest()


def record(sub: dict, cnt: dict, inputs: dict) -> dict:
    """The run in the shape of the repository's data record, as k48_wait_test reads it."""
    return {
        "meta": {"chains": inputs["chains"], "groups": inputs["groups"], "waits_dt": sub["waits_dt"],
                 "T_M": {"per_chain": sub["T_M"], "dt_s": sub["dt_s"]}, "seeds": inputs["seeds"]},
        "fixed_before_the_data": {"margin": inputs["margin"], "informative_floor": inputs["informative_floor"],
                                  "reference_wait_dt": inputs["reference_wait_dt"]},
        "labels": cnt.get("labels", sub["labels"]),
        "counts": cnt["counts"],
    }


def utc(stamp: str) -> datetime:
    return datetime.fromisoformat(stamp).astimezone(timezone.utc)


def selftest() -> None:
    sub = json.loads((K48_DIR / "submit-48.json").read_text())
    cnt = json.loads((K48_DIR / "results-48-counts.json").read_text())
    k48_inputs = json.loads((K48_DIR / "inputs.json").read_text())
    inputs = {"chains": k48_inputs["chains"], "groups": k48_inputs["groups"], "margin": 0.15, "informative_floor": 0.2,
              "reference_wait_dt": 850, "seeds": {"joint": 48, "bootstrap_A": 4848043, "bootstrap_B": 4848, "n_boot": 10_000}}
    r = reuse.k48_wait_test(record(sub, cnt, inputs))
    old = json.loads((K48_DIR / "results-48.json").read_text())
    worst = 0.0
    for n, p in r["prediction"].items():
        for k in ("F_no", "F_ref", "F_pred", "d_M", "dP_R_TM"):
            worst = max(worst, abs(p[k] - old["prediction"][n][k]))
        for k in ("d_M_ci90", "dP_R_TM_ci90"):
            worst = max(worst, *(abs(x - y) for x, y in zip(p[k], old["prediction"][n][k])))
    same = r["H48"] == old["H48"] and r["informative_chains"] == old["informative_chains"]
    print(f"selftest on Kickoff 48: H48 {r['H48']} (archived {old['H48']}); informative {r['informative_chains']}; "
          f"largest difference in F, d_M, dP_R and their intervals {worst:.2e}; {'PASS' if same and worst < 1e-3 else 'FAIL'}")
